{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom curve (stroke 3) and closed the gap at the crossing so both curves feed the tail fins. By the last check about 111 of 115 standing dominoes were connected to the start, with only a few small stubs near the crossing left over. The fish outline (body, forked tail) should read clearly, but I haven't seen the push result or the judge's guess, so I can't say it succeeded. My part was one curve plus one joint. Sofia, Hana and Jack did the nose, top curve, tail fins and cleanup.

Execution: The bottom curve went down cleanly and stayed connected. The crossing was the weak spot. The stray vertical line near it and the pale stubs there probably came from my gap-closing work, and Hana had to take the spike down twice. I told the table it 'wasn't meant to be anything', which was true, but I should have checked what I'd left behind before calling the gap closed. After that I stopped adding anything and kept the chain clean, which was the right call with the clock running down. I also never used inspect on the crossing myself and relied on others' checks.

Collaboration: I stuck to my stroke and followed Sofia's plan. I also said I had the crossing gap in hand while Sofia was bridging it too, which risked doubling up. I flagged that I was handling it, and nothing collided. I accepted Hana's correction about the spike and left the stubs alone. I mostly gave short status updates rather than helping others' lines, even though my curve was done early.

Leadership: This wasn't a leading role for me. Sofia set the plan and Hana and Jack coordinated checks. I helped keep the table calm with a hands-off rule near the end and kept my updates brief. Next time, once my stroke is finished I'd offer to inspect other joints, such as the nose, rather than waiting."}
